# ruff: noqa: F821
# graph_headroom — evolution seed for the dev-continuum-* family.  Identity stays
# outside EVOLVE-BLOCKs; Shinka operators may change only the implementation below.
#
# Why this seed and not `least_allocated` (the dev-medium-hot seed): on this family the
# dependency-blind policies are *infeasible* (worst SLO 0.88 against a 0.90 target), so
# seeding from one would start every arm outside the feasible region and turn the first
# half of every campaign into a feasibility hunt rather than a search.  This seed is the
# most SLO-margined feasible hand-written policy (0.95); it is also the *expensive* one
# (1.27 normalized energy against `latency_greedy`'s 0.83), which is deliberate — the
# search starts feasible and has an explicit, large energy gap to close rather than
# starting at the best baseline with nowhere to go.
POLICY_NAME: str = "graph_headroom"
POLICY_VERSION: str = "1.0.0"

# EVOLVE-BLOCK-START
def resource_score(requested: int, capacity: int) -> int:
    if capacity == 0 or requested > capacity:
        return 0
    return ((capacity - requested) * 100) // capacity

def score(pod: Pod, node: NodeState, ctx: ClusterCtx) -> float:
    cpu = resource_score(node.cpu_allocated + pod.cpu_request, node.cpu_capacity)
    mem = resource_score(node.mem_allocated + pod.mem_request, node.mem_capacity)
    return float((cpu + mem) // 2)

def propose_moves(state: ClusterState, graph: CallGraphCtx, budget: int) -> list[Move]:
    out: list[Move] = []
    return out
# EVOLVE-BLOCK-END

# ruff: noqa: F821
# graph_headroom — evolution seed for the dev-continuum-* family.  Identity stays
# outside EVOLVE-BLOCKs; Shinka operators may change only the implementation below.
#
# Why this seed and not `least_allocated` (the dev-medium-hot seed): on this family the
# dependency-blind policies are *infeasible* (worst SLO 0.88 against a 0.90 target), so
# seeding from one would start every arm outside the feasible region and turn the first
# half of every campaign into a feasibility hunt rather than a search.  This seed is the
# most SLO-margined feasible hand-written policy (0.95); it is also the *expensive* one
# (1.27 normalized energy against `latency_greedy`'s 0.83), which is deliberate — the
# search starts feasible and has an explicit, large energy gap to close rather than
# starting at the best baseline with nowhere to go.
POLICY_NAME: str = "graph_headroom"
POLICY_VERSION: str = "1.0.0"

# EVOLVE-BLOCK-START
def path_cost(pod: Pod, node: NodeState, pods: list[Pod], graph: CallGraphCtx) -> float:
    weighted = 0.0
    weight = 0.0
    worst = 0.0
    for e in range(len(graph.src)):
        other = -1
        if graph.src[e] == pod.id:
            other = graph.dst[e]
        elif graph.dst[e] == pod.id:
            other = graph.src[e]
        if other >= 0 and other != pod.id and graph.rate[e] > 0.0:
            neighbor = pods[other]
            if neighbor.current_node >= 0:
                latency = node.latency_to_ms[neighbor.current_node]
                weighted = weighted + graph.rate[e] * latency
                weight = weight + graph.rate[e]
                worst = max(worst, latency)
    if weight <= 0.0:
        return 0.0
    return weighted / weight + worst

def dynamic_increment(pod: Pod, node: NodeState) -> float:
    dynamic = max(node.power_max_w - node.power_idle_w, 0.0)
    return dynamic * float(pod.cpu_request) / float(max(node.cpu_capacity, 1))

def score(pod: Pod, node: NodeState, ctx: ClusterCtx) -> float:
    if node.suspended:
        return -1000000.0
    cpu_after = float(node.cpu_allocated + pod.cpu_request) / float(max(node.cpu_capacity, 1))
    mem_after = float(node.mem_allocated + pod.mem_request) / float(max(node.mem_capacity, 1))
    peak = max(cpu_after, mem_after)
    if peak > 1.0:
        return -1000000.0
    queue_cost = peak / max(1.0 - peak, 0.02)
    latency_cost = path_cost(pod, node, ctx.pods, ctx.graph) / 45.0
    energy_cost = dynamic_increment(pod, node)
    if node.cpu_allocated == 0 and node.mem_allocated == 0:
        energy_cost = energy_cost + node.power_idle_w
    cost = queue_cost * 0.50 + latency_cost * 0.35 + energy_cost / 120.0 * 0.15
    return -cost

def propose_moves(state: ClusterState, graph: CallGraphCtx, budget: int) -> list[Move]:
    out: list[Move] = []
    if budget <= 0:
        return out
    best_pod = -1
    best_target = -1
    best_saving = 1.0
    for p in range(len(state.pods)):
        pod = state.pods[p]
        eligible = pod.current_node >= 0 and not pod.stateful and not pod.has_pdb
        if eligible:
            source = state.nodes[pod.current_node]
            empties_source = source.cpu_allocated == pod.cpu_request and source.mem_allocated == pod.mem_request
            if source.suspendable and not source.suspended and empties_source:
                source_cpu = float(source.cpu_allocated) / float(max(source.cpu_capacity, 1))
                source_mem = float(source.mem_allocated) / float(max(source.mem_capacity, 1))
                source_peak = max(source_cpu, source_mem)
                source_latency = path_cost(pod, source, state.pods, graph)
                source_power = source.power_idle_w + dynamic_increment(pod, source)
                for n in range(len(state.nodes)):
                    target = state.nodes[n]
                    candidate = n != pod.current_node and not target.suspended
                    if candidate:
                        cpu_after = float(target.cpu_allocated + pod.cpu_request) / float(max(target.cpu_capacity, 1))
                        mem_after = float(target.mem_allocated + pod.mem_request) / float(max(target.mem_capacity, 1))
                        target_peak = max(cpu_after, mem_after)
                        target_latency = path_cost(pod, target, state.pods, graph)
                        target_power = dynamic_increment(pod, target)
                        if target.cpu_allocated == 0 and target.mem_allocated == 0:
                            target_power = target_power + target.power_idle_w
                        saving = source_power - target_power
                        safe = target_peak < 0.65 and target_peak <= source_peak and target_latency <= source_latency
                        if safe and saving > best_saving:
                            best_pod = pod.id
                            best_target = n
                            best_saving = saving
    if best_pod >= 0:
        out.append(move_pod(best_pod, best_target))
    return out
# EVOLVE-BLOCK-END

# ruff: noqa: F821
# graph_headroom — evolution seed for the dev-continuum-* family.  Identity stays
# outside EVOLVE-BLOCKs; Shinka operators may change only the implementation below.
#
# Why this seed and not `least_allocated` (the dev-medium-hot seed): on this family the
# dependency-blind policies are *infeasible* (worst SLO 0.88 against a 0.90 target), so
# seeding from one would start every arm outside the feasible region and turn the first
# half of every campaign into a feasibility hunt rather than a search.  This seed is the
# most SLO-margined feasible hand-written policy (0.95); it is also the *expensive* one
# (1.27 normalized energy against `latency_greedy`'s 0.83), which is deliberate — the
# search starts feasible and has an explicit, large energy gap to close rather than
# starting at the best baseline with nowhere to go.
POLICY_NAME: str = "graph_headroom"
POLICY_VERSION: str = "1.0.0"

# EVOLVE-BLOCK-START
def peak_after(pod: Pod, node: NodeState) -> float:
    cpu = float(node.cpu_allocated + pod.cpu_request) / float(max(node.cpu_capacity, 1))
    mem = float(node.mem_allocated + pod.mem_request) / float(max(node.mem_capacity, 1))
    return max(cpu, mem)

def dynamic_increment(pod: Pod, node: NodeState) -> float:
    dynamic = max(node.power_max_w - node.power_idle_w, 0.0)
    return dynamic * float(pod.cpu_request) / float(max(node.cpu_capacity, 1))

def admission_power(pod: Pod, node: NodeState) -> float:
    power = dynamic_increment(pod, node)
    if node.cpu_allocated == 0 and node.mem_allocated == 0:
        power = power + max(node.power_idle_w, 0.0)
    return power

def path_cost(pod: Pod, node: NodeState, pods: list[Pod], graph: CallGraphCtx) -> float:
    weighted = 0.0
    weight = 0.0
    incoming_worst = 0.0
    outgoing_worst = 0.0
    for e in range(len(graph.src)):
        other = -1
        outgoing = False
        if graph.src[e] == pod.id:
            other = graph.dst[e]
            outgoing = True
        elif graph.dst[e] == pod.id:
            other = graph.src[e]
        if other >= 0 and other != pod.id and graph.rate[e] > 0.0:
            neighbor = pods[other]
            if neighbor.current_node >= 0:
                latency = max(node.latency_to_ms[neighbor.current_node], 0.0)
                weighted = weighted + graph.rate[e] * latency
                weight = weight + graph.rate[e]
                if outgoing:
                    outgoing_worst = max(outgoing_worst, latency)
                else:
                    incoming_worst = max(incoming_worst, latency)
    if weight <= 0.0:
        return 0.0
    return 0.50 * weighted / weight + incoming_worst + outgoing_worst

def score(pod: Pod, node: NodeState, ctx: ClusterCtx) -> float:
    if node.suspended:
        return -1000000.0
    peak = peak_after(pod, node)
    if peak > 1.0:
        return -1000000.0

    cpu = float(node.cpu_allocated + pod.cpu_request) / float(max(node.cpu_capacity, 1))
    cpu_queue = cpu / max(1.0 - cpu, 0.02)
    peak_queue = peak / max(1.0 - peak, 0.02)
    pressure = max(peak - 0.45, 0.0)
    latency = path_cost(pod, node, ctx.pods, ctx.graph) / 45.0

    # Bound the influence of energy so activation savings cannot dominate
    # substantial queueing or critical-path penalties.
    power = admission_power(pod, node)
    energy = power / (120.0 + power)
    energy_weight = 0.04
    if peak <= 0.45 and latency <= 0.35:
        energy_weight = 0.20

    cost = 0.25 * peak + 0.35 * cpu_queue + 0.15 * peak_queue
    cost = cost + 2.50 * latency + 12.0 * pressure * pressure
    cost = cost + energy_weight * energy
    return -cost

def propose_moves(state: ClusterState, graph: CallGraphCtx, budget: int) -> list[Move]:
    out: list[Move] = []
    # The exposed records provide no cumulative disruption accounting or
    # remaining allowance. Repeated windows must not spend an unknown budget.
    # Placement-time consolidation supplies energy savings without migrations.
    return out
# EVOLVE-BLOCK-END
